questions.stem: What are the three tiers of Lifecycle Management? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three tiers of Lifecycle Management are: Know what you have (C) — gaining visibility into your asset inventory; Improve management controls (D) — enhancing governance and oversight of assets; and Improve efficiency (E) — optimizing processes across the lifecycle. Options A ('Know what you don't have') and B ('Increase onboarding controls') are not standard tiers in ServiceNow's lifecycle management framework.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow role enables the user to perform actions related to incident, problem, change, and configuration management?
questions.explanation: The itil role (C) enables users to perform actions related to incident, problem, change, and configuration management. This is the standard ITSM role that grants access to core IT service management modules. procurement_user is for procurement, inventory_admin is for inventory management, discovery_admin is for Discovery, and asset is for asset management — none of these provide the combined ITSM module access that itil provides.

questions.stem: Which plugins for asset management functionality are inactive by default? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The asset management plugins that are inactive by default are Expense Line (A), Depreciation (D), and Cost Management (E). These are optional financial plugins that must be explicitly activated. Hardware Asset Management (B) and Procurement (C) are also separate plugins but are more core to HAM. My Assets (F) is part of the base platform. The three financial-focused plugins (Expense Line, Depreciation, Cost Management) require deliberate activation.

questions.stem: What is the third tier of the capability blueprint?
questions.explanation: The four tiers of the ITAM Capability Blueprint are: Tier 1 — Trustworthy Data, Tier 2 — Practical Management, Tier 3 — Operational Integration, Tier 4 — Strategic Conformance. The third tier is Operational Integration (D), which focuses on integrating asset management processes with other operational workflows. This tier bridges practical management with strategic alignment.

questions.stem: Which is NOT a component of a hardware asset's lifecycle?
questions.explanation: The standard hardware asset lifecycle in ServiceNow includes Request, Procure, Receive, Dispose (and stages in between like Deploy/In Use). 'Consume' (C) is NOT a lifecycle stage for hardware assets — it applies to consumable assets instead. Hardware assets are tracked individually throughout their lifecycle, while consumables are tracked in bulk by quantity and are 'consumed' when used.

questions.stem: The Hardware Asset Management (HAM) application expands baseline ITSM Asset Management with which features? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: HAM expands baseline ITSM Asset Management with: Mobile Asset Receiving (A) — receiving assets via mobile app; Hardware Model Normalization (C) — standardizing model data against the Content Service; and Hardware Asset Dashboard (D) — providing analytics and KPIs. Stockrooms (E), Asset & Model Records (F), and Mobile My Assets (B) are already part of baseline ITSM Asset Management, not HAM-specific expansions.

questions.stem: Expected outcomes of IT asset management (ITAM) include which of the following? (Choose three.)

options.text: Integrates with business services via the Service Catalog from request through to disposal
Leverages IT Service Management (ITSM) to manage the lifecycle of assets as they pass through their useful life as configuration items (CIs)
Provides input into, aligns with, and follows corporate governance
Improves application privacy and security adherence
Leverages Service Mapping to predict service impact

questions.explanation: Expected ITAM outcomes include: integrating with business services via Service Catalog from request through disposal (A); leveraging ITSM to manage lifecycle of assets as CIs (B); and providing input into and aligning with corporate governance (C). Option D about application privacy/security adherence is not a primary ITAM outcome — that belongs to security management. Option E about Service Mapping predictions is also not an ITAM outcome.

questions.stem: What is the difference between ITAM personas and ITAM Roles? (Choose four.)

options.text: A user may have multiple roles, but a single persona
Roles control access to features in the product
Personas represent types of users of the product
Personas control access to features in the product
Roles represent types of users of the product
A user may have multiple roles and personas

questions.explanation: The key differences are: A user may have multiple roles but a single persona (A); Roles control access to features in the product (B); Personas represent types of users of the product (C); A user may have multiple roles and personas (F). Options D and E reverse the definitions — personas don't control access (roles do), and roles don't represent user types (personas do). Personas are conceptual user archetypes, while roles are technical access controls.

questions.stem: Hamm is a member of the Asset Managers group which has the ham_admin role assigned to it. Based on this role alone, which of the following operations can Hamm perform? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: With the ham_admin role, Hamm can: Revert normalization results (A) — ham_admin manages normalization; Create and delete asset records (B) — full CRUD on assets; Create purchase orders (C) — ham_admin includes procurement capabilities; Import assets (E) — ham_admin can perform data imports. Creating flows (D) requires flow_designer or admin role, and adding Service Catalog entries (F) requires catalog_admin role — neither is included in ham_admin by default.

questions.stem: What information would you track for a configuration item (CI) versus an asset? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Configuration items (CIs) track Lifecycle (B) information — their operational state and history — and Operational (D) details like IP address, OS, CPU, and memory. Assets track Financial (A) and Contractual (C) information. Relationship (E) data is tracked in the CMDB for CIs but is not a distinguishing characteristic asked here. The question asks what you'd specifically track for a CI versus an asset, and operational/lifecycle data is CI-centric.

questions.stem: A component is considered an IT asset vs. a configuration item (CI) when you want to do which of the following? (Choose three.)

options.text: Manage its procurement, maintenance, or retirement
Track its monetary value or costs
Manage its associated license, warranty, or lease contracts
Know its relationships to other assets in the CMDB

questions.explanation: A component is considered an IT asset when you want to: Manage its procurement, maintenance, or retirement (A); Track its monetary value or costs (C); Manage its associated license, warranty, or lease contracts (D). These are all financial and lifecycle management concerns that define asset management. Tracking operational information (B) and knowing relationships to other items in the CMDB (E) are CI concerns, not asset-specific.

questions.stem: Which of the following are considered assets? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Assets in ServiceNow include: Facilities (A) — buildings and physical locations have financial value and lifecycle; Hardware (C) — computers, servers, network equipment; Software entitlements (D) — licenses and entitlements that have value. Contracts (B) are not assets themselves — they are associated with assets. Software distributions (E) are the installable media/packages, not the entitlement/license which is the actual asset.

questions.stem: What is the default display name for an asset?

options.text: An automatically generated combination of serial number and model category
An automatically generated combination of asset tag and model
An automatically generated combination of serial number and model
An automatically generated combination of asset tag and model category

questions.explanation: The default display name for an asset is an automatically generated combination of asset tag and model (B). When an asset record is created, the system automatically generates the display name by combining the asset tag number with the model name. The display name does not use serial number or model category in its auto-generation — it specifically uses the asset tag identifier and the model reference.

questions.stem: What is the default state of a newly created asset?
questions.explanation: The default state of a newly created asset is 'In stock' (D). When an asset is first created in ServiceNow, it enters the In stock state, indicating it is available in inventory but not yet deployed or assigned. 'On order' (C) applies when assets are created from purchase orders before receipt. 'In use' (A) is set when assigned to a user. 'Consumed' (B) applies to consumable assets after use.

questions.stem: What is the impact of a customer opting out of the ServiceNow Content Service for specific models?

options.text: Unrecognized data doesn't get sent to the ServiceNow Content Service and the customer doesn't receive Content Library updates
Unrecognized data doesn't get sent to the ServiceNow Content Service
Unrecognized data is sent to the ServiceNow Content Service, but is now encrypted
Customer doesn't receive Content Library updates

questions.explanation: When a customer opts out of the ServiceNow Content Service for specific models, the customer doesn't receive Content Library updates for those models (D). Opting out means the system will no longer download normalization data and lifecycle information for those specific models from ServiceNow's Content Service. Unrecognized data is not 'sent' to the Content Service — the Content Service pushes data to instances, so options about sending data (A, B, C) mischaracterize the flow.

questions.stem: What fields does the ServiceNow Content Service normalize or enrich? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The ServiceNow Content Service normalizes or enriches: Lifecycle (A) — end-of-life, end-of-sale dates; Device type (B) — categorization like laptop, desktop, server; Manufacturer (C) — standardized manufacturer names; Hardware model (F) — normalized model information. Memory (D) and Asset tag (E) are instance-specific data that the Content Service cannot normalize — they are unique per-device attributes discovered or entered locally.

questions.stem: What is the process of restructuring data to maintain consistency?
questions.explanation: Normalization (B) is the process of restructuring data to maintain consistency. In the context of HAM, Hardware Model Normalization standardizes manufacturer names, model names, and other attributes so that data is consistent across the organization. Integration (A) connects systems, Discovery (C) finds CIs on the network, and Service Mapping (D) maps business services to infrastructure — none of these are about data consistency/restructuring.

questions.stem: What are ways to measure trustworthy data? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Trustworthy data is measured by: Plausibility (B) — data appears reasonable; Credibility (C) — data comes from reliable sources; Dependability (D) — data is consistent and can be relied upon; Reliability (F) — data produces consistent results over time. Sustainability (A) and Transferability (E) are not standard measures of data trustworthiness in the ITAM framework. The four measures focus on whether data can be believed and relied upon for decision-making.

questions.stem: Any normalization that has occurred on a model can be reverted by using this feature.
questions.explanation: Normalization can be reverted using the Revert Normalization UI Action (D). On the model record, selecting 'Revert Normalization' reverts all normalization changes and deactivates the normalization rule. When the scheduled job runs again, the model is reprocessed with active rules. This is a UI Action on the model form, not a business rule, scheduled job, or permanent restriction — normalizations can always be reverted.

questions.stem: Which of these tables are installed with Hardware Model Normalization? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Hardware Model Normalization installs: Device Type (A) — categorizes hardware/consumable models into types like laptop, desktop, server; Hardware Normalize Key (C) — stores normalization rule keys used for matching; Hardware Model Library (D) — contains reference data from the Content Service. Hardware Manufacturer (B) is part of the base CMDB/model system, and Device Name (E) is not a standard normalization table.

questions.stem: To perform hardware model normalization, which three fields from the hardware model record are used to set the normalized display name?

options.text: Name, Asset tracking unit, Model number
Asset tracking unit, Manufacturer, Model category
Asset tracking unit, Manufacturer, Model number

questions.explanation: During hardware model normalization, three fields from the hardware model record are used to set the normalized display name: Name, Manufacturer, and Model number (B). The normalization process compares these three key attributes against the Content Service to produce a standardized display name. Asset tracking unit and Model category are model properties but are not used in the normalization display name calculation.

questions.stem: What is the global standard for product recognition used during hardware model normalization?
questions.explanation: UNSPSC — United Nations Standard Products and Services Code (C) — is the global standard for product recognition used during hardware model normalization. UNSPSC provides a hierarchical classification system for products and services used worldwide. IAPSO (A) is a UN procurement agency, UPC (B) is a barcode standard, ECCMA (D) is an e-commerce organization, and NIGP (E) is a public procurement code — none are the primary product classification standard used in HAM normalization.

questions.stem: During hardware model normalization, a hardware asset is set to a normalization status of, "Partially Normalized". What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The model name is missing from the hardware model record.
The model number is missing from the hardware model record.
The model product is missing from the hardware model record.
The model manufacturer is missing from the hardware model record.

questions.explanation: A 'Partially Normalized' status means the model number is missing from the hardware model record (B). For a model to be fully normalized, it needs manufacturer details AND a model number (and optionally a model name). If the manufacturer is present but the model number is missing, the status will be Partially Normalized. The model name (A) is optional for full normalization — it helps but is not required. Model product (C) is not a standard field.

questions.stem: What information should be tracked in an asset record? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: An asset record tracks Financial information (B) — cost, depreciation, residual value — and Contractual information (D) — warranties, leases, maintenance agreements. These are the two primary data types that distinguish asset records from CIs. Physical resources (A) and Logical relationships (E) are CMDB/CI concerns. Operational details (C) like IP address and OS are also CI-specific attributes rather than asset-tracked data.

questions.stem: Once the content update adds hardware lifecycle data to your instance, can it be deleted?

options.text: No, it cannot unless the lifecycle stage is EOL
Yes, it can be deleted or deactivated

questions.explanation: Once the content update adds hardware lifecycle data to your instance, it can be deleted or deactivated (D). Lifecycle data received from the Hardware Asset Management Content Service can be managed by administrators who can delete or deactivate lifecycle records as needed. The Content Service does not lock data — administrators retain full control over their instance data including the ability to override or remove lifecycle values.

questions.stem: What feature does the Hardware Asset Management (HAM) application use to fully normalize hardware models?
questions.explanation: The HAM application uses Mapping assist (B) to fully normalize hardware models. Mapping assist helps map and align hardware model data with the Content Service to achieve full normalization. Transform mappings (A) are used for data imports, not normalization. Normalization transformation (C), Normalization mappings (D), and Transform normalization (E) are not standard ServiceNow features for HAM normalization.

questions.stem: During normalization, what is the most common cause for hardware models to generate a status of Match Not Found?
questions.explanation: The most common cause for hardware models to generate a 'Match Not Found' status during normalization is Missing data (D). When key fields like manufacturer, model name, or model number are missing or incomplete on the hardware model record, the Content Service cannot find a match. Missing transform map (A) and Invalid transform map (C) relate to data imports rather than normalization. Plugin issues (B) would cause errors, not specific match failures.

questions.stem: Which values does the "Asset tracking strategy" field provide to affect individual models? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The 'Asset tracking strategy' field on individual models provides three values: Don't create assets (B) — prevents auto-creation of assets from CIs; Leave to category (D) — defers to the model category's tracking strategy setting; Create assets (E) — forces asset creation from CIs. Create consumable asset (A) and Merge CI (C) are not valid values for this field. The strategy controls whether assets are automatically created when CIs of that model are discovered.

questions.stem: When activating Hardware Asset Management (HAM) in an instance already running Field Service Management (FSM), how do you configure asset tasks for existing incident, change, and work order flows?

options.text: No configuration is required: asset tasks automatically activate behind the scenes
Activate HAM, then run scheduled job "Asset - Create FSM asset tasks" to insert the asset tasks
Activate HAM and then re-run the scheduled FSM jobs
Stop the scheduled FSM jobs, activate HAM, then restart the scheduled FSM jobs

questions.explanation: When activating HAM in an instance already running FSM, no configuration is required — asset tasks automatically activate behind the scenes (A). The HAM plugin includes lifecycle automation flows that integrate with existing ITSM/FSM workflows. When HAM is activated, the asset task functionality is automatically enabled and works with existing incident, change, and work order flows without manual configuration or job execution.

questions.stem: When a hardware asset is retired (e.g., a server), what happens to any existing software allocations on that asset?

options.text: The software allocations remain with the hardware asset and need to be reclaimed manually.
The software allocations are automatically returned back into inventory.
The software allocations are removed from the asset, but not returned to inventory.
The behavior is controlled by the configurable system property glide.ham.retire_reclaim_sw().
The behavior is controlled by the configurable system property glide.ham.retire_sw().

questions.explanation: When a hardware asset is retired, the software allocations are automatically returned back into inventory (B). ServiceNow's HAM retirement process includes automatic reclamation of software licenses allocated to the retired hardware. This ensures software entitlements are not wasted when hardware is decommissioned. The allocations don't remain for manual reclamation (A), aren't just removed without returning (C), and there is no configurable system property controlling this behavior.

questions.stem: With regard to Contract Management notifications, what is the most important contract dale to be aware of?
questions.explanation: The most important contract date for Contract Management notifications is the Expire date (C). The system sends reminders to contract administrators about upcoming contract expirations so they can renew or renegotiate. By default, notifications are sent at intervals leading up to the expiration date (90, 60, 30 days before, and day of expiration). While renew (B) and extend (A) dates exist, the expire date drives the critical notification workflow.

questions.stem: Inventory audit results provide easy visibility into the reconciliation of scanned assets to the existing inventory. What audit statuses are displayed as part of the results? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The asset inventory audit displays four result statuses: New (C) — assets scanned that have no existing record; Scanned and not expected (D) — assets scanned but not on the expected list; Scanned and expected (E) — assets scanned that match the expected inventory; Expected and not found (F) — assets expected but not scanned. 'Scanned' (A) alone is not a result status, and 'Not found' (B) is incomplete — the full status is 'Expected and not found'.

questions.stem: How can you automate the replenishment of stock levels?
questions.explanation: Stock Rules (D) automate the replenishment of stock levels. Stock rules define criteria so that when inventory of a particular asset in a stockroom reaches a specified threshold, the system automatically creates transfer orders to restock from another stockroom or purchase orders from a vendor. Transfer Rules (A) and Stock Filters (C) are not standard features. Transfer Orders (B) are the mechanism created by stock rules, not the automation trigger itself.

questions.stem: What are baseline asset states? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The baseline asset states in ServiceNow are: In Stock (A) — asset is in inventory and available; Consumed (B) — for consumable assets that have been used; Retired (C) — asset has been decommissioned. These are three of the standard states in the asset lifecycle. Duplicate (D) is not an asset state — it's a data quality issue. Exported (E) is not a standard asset state in ServiceNow's asset management framework.

questions.stem: What field must an agent complete when resolving an incident in order for the HAM asset tasks to automatically update all configuration item (CI) and asset records associated to the Incident?
questions.explanation: When resolving an incident, the agent must complete the Asset Action (D) field for HAM asset tasks to automatically update all CI and asset records associated with the incident. This field triggers the appropriate asset task flow (swap, retire, etc.) which then updates the related asset and CI records. The other options (Asset and CI Action, Asset-CI Task Action, Asset Task Action) are not the correct field names in the incident resolution form.

questions.stem: Which mobile app allows the user to conduct an inventory audit?
questions.explanation: The ServiceNow Agent mobile app (A) — also called Now Agent — allows users to conduct inventory audits by scanning asset barcodes. The Agent mobile app includes functionality for creating assets, performing inventory audits, and receiving assets. Mobile My Assets (D) is for end users to view their assigned assets. Mobile My Inventory (B), Mobile Hardware Asset Management (C), and ServiceNow Inventory mobile app (E) are not actual ServiceNow mobile apps.

questions.stem: When running an asset audit, you receive the result of 10 "Scanned and expected" assets. What does this mean?

options.text: You expected 10 assets in your inventory and scanned 10 assets during your audit, but none of them are on your expected inventory list.
You expected 10 assets in your inventory and scanned these 10 assets during your audit.
You expected 10 assets during your audit inventory and scanned 10 assets, but none of them have a record in your ServiceNow instance.
You scanned 10 assets in your inventory, but none of them were on your expected inventory list.

questions.explanation: 'Scanned and expected' means you expected these assets in your inventory and scanned them during the audit (B). This is the ideal outcome — the physical scan matches the expected inventory records. Option A incorrectly states they were not on the expected list. Option C incorrectly says they have no record. Option D is not the correct definition. 'Scanned and expected' confirms inventory accuracy for those 10 assets.

questions.stem: During an audit, when is the Expected Assets list populated in the asset audit form?

options.text: When the nightly scheduled job runs
Pre-populated by the asset manager before audit
When the asset manager Submits the results

questions.explanation: The Expected Assets list is populated when scanning begins (C). When an asset audit starts and the first scan is initiated, the system automatically populates the Expected Assets related list based on the stockroom or location being audited. It pulls all known assets assigned to that stockroom/location. It is not populated by the nightly job (A), after scanning completes (B), pre-populated by the manager (D), or when results are submitted (E).

questions.stem: Which of the following are valid substates of the Retired state? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Valid substates of the Retired state are: Disposed (A) — asset has been disposed of; Donated (B) — asset was donated; Pending Disposal (E) — asset is awaiting disposal processing; Sold (F) — asset was sold. Vendor Credit (C) is not a standard retired substate. Destroyed (D) is not a baseline substate — disposal methods like destruction are tracked differently. The four valid substates cover the main retirement outcomes.

questions.stem:
When a stock manager receives a new delivery of consumables, what happens if all the following fields match another record in the stockroom?
• Assigned to
• Model
• Model category
• State
• Stockroom
• Substate

options.text: The stock manager must create a separate model record if the cost per item is more/less
The data is automatically merged to create a blended quantity and cost
The data is automatically created in a new record if the cost per item is more/less
The stock manager must merge the consumable records to create a blended quantity and cost

questions.explanation: When a new delivery of consumables matches all key fields (Assigned to, Model, Model category, State, Stockroom, Substate), the data is automatically merged to create a blended quantity and cost (B). Consumables in ServiceNow are tracked in bulk, so when identical consumables arrive, the system merges them into the existing record, combining quantities and calculating a blended average cost. This is a core feature of consumable asset management.

questions.stem: How does an end user determine what consumables they have consumed?

options.text: Navigate to Asset > Hardware Asset Dashboard
Navigate to Self-Service > My Hardware Asset Dashboard

questions.explanation: End users can determine what consumables they have consumed by navigating to Self-Service > My Assets (B). The My Assets view shows all assets assigned to the user, including both hardware and consumable assets. There is no separate 'My Consumables' module (A). The Hardware Asset Dashboard (C, D) is for asset managers, not end users. My Assets is the self-service portal where users see everything assigned to them.

questions.stem: When using transfer orders to move multiple assets from a single stockroom to another, how should each asset be listed?

options.text: Each asset should be listed as a transfer order line on the transfer order
Each asset should be listed in a transfer order task on the transfer order
Each asset should be listed as a transfer order line on the transfer order task
Each asset should be listed in an individual transfer order

questions.explanation: When using transfer orders to move multiple assets from one stockroom to another, each asset should be listed as a transfer order line on the transfer order (A). Transfer order lines are the child records that specify individual assets being transferred. Each line represents one asset (or one consumable quantity). Transfer order tasks are automatically created from lines to track stages — they are not where assets are listed. Individual transfer orders per asset (D) would be inefficient.

questions.stem: What happens to the associated assets when you cancel a transfer order line on a transfer order?

options.text: The asset(s) on the order line are released, but their state remains Pre-allocated
The asset(s) on the order line are released and they can be attached to another transfer order
All assets on the transfer order are released, but their state remains Pre-allocated
A transfer order line cannot be cancelled once it is in a state of Ready for fulfillment
All assets on the transfer order are released and they can be attached to another transfer order

questions.explanation: When you cancel a transfer order line, the assets on that order line are released and can be attached to another transfer order (B). Cancellation frees the assets from the pre-allocation so they become available for other transfer orders or assignments. Option A is wrong because the state does not remain Pre-allocated. Option C incorrectly states ALL assets on the order are released (only the cancelled line's assets). Option D is incorrect because lines can be cancelled.

questions.stem: When transferring non-consumable assets between stockrooms, how must they be transferred?

options.text: No more than 10% of the source stockroom's inventory
As a single entity with a quantity of one

questions.explanation: Non-consumable assets must be transferred as a single entity with a quantity of one (C). Unlike consumable assets which can be transferred in bulk quantities, non-consumable assets correspond to individual asset records in the system and must be tracked individually. Each non-consumable asset has a unique asset tag and identity, so it must be transferred one at a time with quantity of one per transfer order line.

questions.stem: When disposing of an IT asset through a vendor, what documentation should be attached to the retired asset's record as proof of adherence to environmental, regulatory, and legal requirements?
questions.explanation: When disposing of an IT asset through a vendor, a Certificate of destruction (C) should be attached to the retired asset's record as proof of adherence to environmental, regulatory, and legal requirements. This certificate verifies that the vendor properly destroyed/disposed of the asset including data sanitization. Certificate of disposal (D) sounds plausible but 'destruction' is the standard industry term for the compliance documentation.

questions.stem: You may adjust a contract when it is in which of the following states? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: A contract can be adjusted when it is in Active (A) or Extended (B) states. Active contracts are the primary state where adjustments like adding assets, modifying terms, or updating financial details are permitted. Extended contracts are still 'live' and can also be adjusted. Canceled (C), Expired (D), and Renewed (E) contracts are in terminal or completed states where direct adjustments are not applicable.

questions.stem: Which catalogs support the request and procurement process? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Three catalogs support the request and procurement process: Product Catalog (A) — contains all hardware and consumable models available for procurement; Service Catalog (D) — enables end users to request assets through a self-service portal; Procurement Catalog (E) — specifically for procurement sourcing from vendors. Vendor Catalog (B) is not a standard ServiceNow catalog name, and Asset Catalog (C) is not a separate catalog type.

questions.stem: What are the three types of catalogs in ServiceNow? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three types of catalogs in ServiceNow are: Product Catalog (A) — where models are defined and managed for procurement; Vendor Catalog (D) — catalogs maintained by vendors for sourcing; Service Catalog (E) — the self-service portal for requesting items. Consumable Catalog (B) and Asset Catalog (C) are not standard separate catalog types in ServiceNow. The Product, Vendor, and Service catalogs form the three-catalog framework.

questions.stem: The Stock Rule Runner scheduled job replenishes stock in a stockroom__________.

options.text: When stock is less than the threshold specified in the stock rule
By creating a purchase orders to restock from other stockrooms
By creating transfer orders to restock from other stockrooms
By notifying the stockroom manager of new transfer orders

questions.explanation: The Stock Rule Runner scheduled job replenishes stock in a stockroom when stock is less than the threshold specified in the stock rule (A). The job runs daily to check if inventory has reached the threshold, then triggers restocking actions. It doesn't create purchase orders by default (B) — it creates transfer orders or tasks. Option C partially describes one restocking option but doesn't capture the trigger condition. Option D is incomplete.

questions.stem: When creating a list report that groups all assets by product model, which table is used?
questions.explanation: When creating a list report that groups all assets by product model, the alm_hardware table (D) is used. This table stores hardware asset records and includes the model reference field needed for grouping. alm_asset (A) is the parent asset table but is too broad. alm_model (B) is the model table itself, not an asset table. alm_model_category (C) is for model categories. For hardware asset reports grouped by model, alm_hardware is the correct starting table.

questions.stem: Assets can be scanned and created in ServiceNow via the Agent mobile application in which scenarios? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a single asset via barcode scan
Receive one or multiple assets from a purchase order
Create multiple assets listed on a contract PDF scan
Create a single asset via Name search

questions.explanation: Assets can be scanned and created via the Agent mobile app in two scenarios: Create a single asset via barcode scan (A) — scan a barcode to create a new asset record; Receive one or multiple assets from a purchase order (B) — scan assets during the receiving process for a PO. Creating assets from contract PDF scans (C) is not a supported feature. Creating via Name search (D) is not a scanning scenario — it's a manual search, not a scan operation.

questions.stem: When viewing the Model Management tab of the Hardware Asset dashboard, you see that several models are reported as Match Not Found. What are potential causes of this? (Choose three.)

options.text: You have opted out of the Content Service
The content is not available from the Content Service
Your model form contains a good Model number, but a bad model Name
Something on your model form may be badly formatted
The content has not been downloaded from the Content Service

questions.explanation: Potential causes for Match Not Found on the Model Management tab include: You have opted out of the Content Service (A) — no data to match against; The content is not available from the Content Service (B) — the model doesn't exist in ServiceNow's library; Something on your model form may be badly formatted (D) — typos or formatting issues prevent matching. Option C states a good model number with bad name, but match failures are caused by ALL fields being unmatchable, not just name with good number. Option E about not downloaded content would show different status.

questions.stem: Which of the following are components of the asset request structure? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Components of the asset request structure include: Transfer orders (B) — to move assets from stockrooms to fulfill requests; Purchase orders (D) — to procure assets from vendors when not in stock; Catalog tasks (E) — generated from service catalog requests that drive the fulfillment process. Procurement orders (A) and Stock order tasks (C) are not standard component names in the ServiceNow asset request structure.

questions.stem: What is the primary goal of the Inventory tab of the Hardware Asset Management dashboard?

options.text: Help the asset manager generate reports
Show the value from maintaining inventory
Help the stock manager process transfer orders
Show the value from bulk purchasing
Help the asset manager process purchase orders

questions.explanation: The primary goal of the Inventory tab on the Hardware Asset Management dashboard is to show the value from maintaining inventory (B). It provides visibility into stock levels, audit results, and warehouse health metrics that demonstrate the benefits of good inventory management. It is not primarily for generating reports (A), processing transfer orders (C), showing bulk purchasing value (D), or processing purchase orders (E) — those functions exist elsewhere.

questions.stem: What do certification filters define?

options.text: The percentage of tasks required for the certification to be considered complete
What fields are displayed for certification

questions.explanation: Certification filters define the assets to be certified (C). Filters specify which records should be included in the data certification process based on criteria like location, model category, assigned user, or other attributes. The percentage of tasks (A) is a certification setting, not a filter. When the certification runs (B) is defined by the schedule. What fields are displayed (D) is defined by the certification template, not the filter.

questions.stem: Which features are part of the ServiceNow Mobile App? (Choose two.)

options.text: Provides end users visibility to their assigned hardware
Provides users visibility to their disposed consumables
Enables end users to log incidents for their assigned assets

questions.explanation: The ServiceNow Mobile App (Now Mobile) provides: visibility to assigned hardware for end users (A) — users can see their assets in My Assets; and enables end users to log incidents for their assigned assets (D) — users can report issues with their devices. Reclamation of mobile devices (B) is an admin function not available in the end-user mobile app. Viewing disposed consumables (C) is not a mobile app feature.

questions.stem: What information would you find on the End of Life tab of the Hardware Asset dashboard? (Choose two.)

options.text: New hardware assets found by audits
Consumable models up for End of Life

questions.explanation: The End of Life tab on the Hardware Asset dashboard shows: Hardware asset disposal status (A) — tracking which assets are in various disposal stages; Hardware assets disposed year-to-date (C) — showing disposal volume metrics. New hardware found by audits (B) appears on the Inventory tab. Consumable models up for End of Life (D) would be on the Model Management tab, not the EOL tab which focuses on hardware asset disposal tracking.

questions.stem: What are some examples of operational expenses of managing an asset throughout its lifecycle? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Operational expenses of managing an asset throughout its lifecycle include: Replacement parts (A) — ongoing costs to repair and maintain; Maintenance agreements (C) — recurring costs for service contracts. Storage costs (B) are typically a one-time or facility cost, not an asset operational expense. Warranty costs (D) are original costs included at purchase, not ongoing operational expenses. Operational expenses are the recurring costs incurred during the asset's useful life.

questions.stem: What is the name of the scheduled job that generates expense lines based on rate cards?
questions.explanation: The scheduled job that generates expense lines based on rate cards is Process FM Costs (C). This Financial Management scheduled job runs to calculate and create expense line records based on the rate cards associated with assets and contracts. Process Daily Costs (A) and Process Daily Allocations (C) are not the correct job names. Process Expense Allocations (D) is also not the correct name for this specific rate card processing job.

questions.stem: How do you calculate residual value?

options.text: Subtract the amortized value from the cost of the asset
Subtract storage and lease cost from the cost of the asset
Subtract the depreciation from the cost of the asset
Subtract the salvage value from the cost of the asset

questions.explanation: Residual value is calculated by subtracting the depreciation from the cost of the asset (C). For example, if an asset costs $1000 and has $500 in accumulated depreciation, the residual value is $500. The ServiceNow platform calculates residual value based on Cost, Depreciation method, and Depreciation effective date fields. Salvage value (D) is a separate concept — it's the estimated value at end of useful life, not subtracted from cost to get residual value.

questions.stem: Configuration items (CIs) track what type of information? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Configuration items (CIs) track Operational (B) information — such as IP address, OS, CPU, memory, and software installations — and Relationship (E) information — how CIs relate to each other and to business services in the CMDB. Financial (A) and Contractual (D) data are tracked by asset records. Lifecycle (C) is tracked by both assets and CIs but is more strongly associated with asset management in this context.

questions.stem: When does an asset’s lifecycle begin?

options.text: When an asset request is fulfilled

questions.explanation: An asset's lifecycle begins upon the asset's request (D). The lifecycle starts at the very first stage when someone requests the asset, before procurement, receipt, or deployment. The request phase initiates the entire lifecycle chain: Request > Procure > Receive > Deploy > Use > Retire. Procurement (C) and fulfillment (A) come after the request. Deployment (B) occurs much later in the lifecycle.

questions.stem: What are the goals of IT asset management (ITAM)? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The goals of IT Asset Management include: Optimize cost (A) — reduce spending and maximize value; Provide decision support (B) — data-driven insights for planning; Improve productivity (C) — streamline workflows and reduce manual effort; Improve operational usage (E) — better utilization of existing assets. Provide financial reporting (D) is a capability, not a primary goal. Track logical relationships (F) is a CMDB/CI concern, not an ITAM goal.

questions.stem: A given collection of methodologies, assets, and templates within Now Create is referred to as what?
questions.explanation: A given collection of methodologies, assets, and templates within Now Create is referred to as a Success pack (C). Success packs are pre-built collections that help customers implement ServiceNow solutions using proven methodologies. Now Create pack (A), Project pack (B), Methodology pack (D), and Asset pack (E) are not the correct terminology for this concept in the Now Create framework.

questions.stem: To access the full spectrum of asset management functionality, which inactive plugins should be installed? (Choose five.)
questions.explanation: The inactive plugins to install for full asset management functionality are: Cost Management (B), Procurement (C), Hardware Asset Management (D), Data Certification (E), and Managed Documents (G). These five plugins extend the base ITSM asset management with financial tracking, procurement processes, HAM features, data quality certification, and document management. Discovery (A) and Service Mapping (F) are ITOM plugins, not ITAM-specific.

questions.stem: What are the four tiers of Capability Blueprint?

options.text: Trustworthy Data, Lifecycle Management, Process Integration, Strategic Conformance
Trustworthy Data, Practical Management, Process Integration, Business Alignment
Trustworthy Data, Practical Management, Operational Integration, Strategic Conformance
Trustworthy Data, Lifecycle Management, Operational integration, Business Alignment

questions.explanation: The four tiers of the Capability Blueprint are: Trustworthy Data, Practical Management, Operational Integration, and Strategic Conformance (C). Tier 1 establishes data quality, Tier 2 implements basic management processes, Tier 3 integrates with operational workflows, and Tier 4 achieves strategic alignment. Options A, B, and D mix incorrect tier names like 'Lifecycle Management' or 'Business Alignment' which are not part of the standard blueprint.

questions.stem: What core table requires migration when extending ITSM Asset Management with Hardware Asset Management?
questions.explanation: When extending ITSM Asset Management with Hardware Asset Management, the alm_asset table (D) requires migration. The HAM plugin extends the base alm_asset table with additional fields for hardware-specific tracking, normalization, and lifecycle management. cmdb_model_category (A) is a model table that doesn't require migration. alm_hardware (B) is already a hardware-specific table. The migration is needed on the core asset table to add HAM capabilities.

questions.stem: How could you quickly determine if you had the Hardware Asset Management (HAM) plugin installed on your instance?

options.text: Check for the Hardware Assets module in the application navigator
Check for the Hardware Asset Dashboard module in the application navigator
Check for the Asset application in the application navigator
Check for the Hardware Asset Management application in the application navigator

questions.explanation: You can quickly determine if the HAM plugin is installed by checking for the Hardware Asset Dashboard module in the application navigator (B). The Hardware Asset Dashboard is a distinctive HAM-specific feature that only appears when the HAM plugin is activated. The generic 'Asset' application (C) exists in baseline ITSM. 'Hardware Assets' module (A) could exist without HAM. The full application name (D) may not appear as a single navigator entry.

questions.stem: A component is considered an IT asset when you want to: (Choose three.)

options.text: Know its relationships to a business service

questions.explanation: A component is considered an IT asset when you want to: Manage its procurement (A) — purchasing lifecycle; Track its incurred costs (D) — financial tracking of value and expenses; Manage its maintenance contracts (E) — warranty, lease, and service agreements. Knowing relationships to a business service (B) is a CI/CMDB concern. Tracking operational information (C) like IP address and OS is also CI-specific. Asset management focuses on financial and contractual aspects.

questions.stem: Which is NOT considered an asset?
questions.explanation: Websites (A) are NOT considered assets in the ITAM framework. Websites are digital services, not physical or licensable items with financial lifecycle tracking. Switches (B), Routers (C), and Buildings (D) are all tangible assets with financial value, maintenance needs, and lifecycle tracking. Software entitlements (E) are also assets representing license ownership. Websites may be CIs but are not managed as assets.

questions.stem: What are model records?

options.text: Models are specific versions or various configurations of an asset
Models are any computer, device, software or service in the CMDB
Models directly associate configuration item (CI) classes with asset classes
Models are anything capable of being owned or controlled to produce economic value

questions.explanation: Models are specific versions or various configurations of an asset (A). A model record represents a particular product — like 'Dell Latitude 5520' or 'HP LaserJet Pro M404n'. Multiple asset records can share the same model. Option B describes CIs, not models. Option C describes model categories (which link CI classes with asset classes). Option D describes assets themselves, not model records.

questions.stem: Which of the following are functions of the model category? (Choose two.)

options.text: Model categories group consumables in the Product Catalog
Model categories determine when to create assets from configuration items (Cls)
Model categories group related assets in the Service Catalog
Model categories provide the link between configuration management and asset management
Model categories provide the link between procurement management and asset management

questions.explanation: Model categories serve two key functions: they determine when to create assets from CIs (B) — the tracking strategy on the category controls automatic asset creation; and they provide the link between configuration management and asset management (D) — model categories bridge CMDB CI classes with asset classes. Grouping in Product Catalog (A) is done by models. Grouping in Service Catalog (C) is done by catalog categories, not model categories.

questions.stem: When does hardware normalization run by default?
questions.explanation: Hardware normalization runs upon saving the model record (D). When you save a hardware or consumable model, the system immediately attempts to normalize it by comparing against the Content Service data. Additionally, the HAM - Hardware Normalization scheduled job runs daily to process models that may have been updated or that need re-evaluation. But the first normalization attempt happens immediately upon save, not on a scheduled basis.

questions.stem: For a model to be fully normalized, what must be added to the model record?
questions.explanation: For a model to be fully normalized, the Manufacturer (C) must be added to the model record, along with a model number. The docs state: 'For a model to be fully normalized, you must add manufacturer details and a model number, and optionally a model name.' Without manufacturer, the model can only be Partially Normalized. Version (A), Owner (B), and Model number (D) — while model number is also needed, the question asks what 'must be added' implying from a partially normalized state where manufacturer is the missing piece.

questions.stem: Which elements are provided by the hardware asset management content service? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The Hardware Asset Management Content Service provides: Manufacturer lifecycle dates (A) — end-of-life, end-of-sale dates; Manufacturer (D) — normalized manufacturer names; Model name (E) — standardized product names. Cost (B) is not provided by the Content Service — costs are instance-specific from procurement. Product warranty (C) is also not provided — warranties are contract-specific. Compatibles (F) is not a Content Service offering.

questions.stem: What hardware asset attribute should you track that is NOT part of a configuration item (CI)?
questions.explanation: Cost (C) is a hardware asset attribute that is NOT part of a configuration item. Cost is financial data tracked on the asset record, not the CI record. IP address (A), CPU (B), Operating system (D), and Memory (E) are all operational attributes tracked on CI records in the CMDB. The fundamental distinction between assets and CIs is that assets track financial/contractual data while CIs track operational/relationship data.

questions.stem: Under which condition does the Now Platform NOT create an asset automatically?
questions.explanation: The Now Platform does NOT automatically create an asset during Model characterization (E). Model characterization is the process of defining model attributes and does not trigger asset creation. Assets are auto-created based on CI discovery and the model category's asset tracking strategy. Configuration normalization (A), Enforced CI verification (B), Data synching (C), and Data justification (D) — Enforced CI Verification specifically prevents auto-creation, requiring manual verification instead.

questions.stem: Which three attributes from a hardware model record are used for setting the normalized display name during hardware model normalization?

options.text: Asset tracking unit, Manufacturer, Model number
Name, Asset tracking unit, Model number
Asset tracking unit, Manufacturer, Model category

questions.explanation: The three attributes from a hardware model record used for setting the normalized display name are Name, Manufacturer, and Model number (C). The normalization process uses these three key fields to match against the Content Service and generate a standardized display name. Asset tracking unit is not used in normalization matching — it determines how assets are created, not how models are normalized.

questions.stem: Which key attribute in the model record does hardware model normalization use to normalize inconsistent manufactures and product names?
questions.explanation: The key attribute in the model record that hardware model normalization uses to normalize inconsistent manufacturers and product names is Model number (D). The model number serves as the primary identifier for matching models against the Content Service library. Even when manufacturer and product names vary in format or spelling, the model number provides a consistent reference point for normalization. Asset tag (A) is unique per asset, not per model.

questions.stem: What plugin offers consistent, good, clean data for the company names of vendors or manufactures?
questions.explanation: The Normalization Data Services Client (com.glide.data_services_canonicalization.client) plugin (D) offers consistent, good, clean data for company names of vendors or manufacturers. This plugin normalizes company/manufacturer names to ensure consistency across the platform. Hardware Model Normalization (A) normalizes model data, not company names specifically. Service Catalog API (B) and Outbound Tracking (C) serve entirely different purposes.

questions.stem: Hardware models may not be fully normalized until updated content is downloaded from the Hardware Model Normalization Content Service. How do you determine if the content has been downloaded?

options.text: Determine if the business rule, Create a Hardware Normalization Download, has been triggered yet or not
Review the Last updated date of the Central Data Service Download Status jobs on the Normalization and Content Service dashboard
Review the Hardware Model Content Service Download section on the Model Management tab of the Hardware Asset dashboard
Query the scheduled job reports to determine if the Hardware Normalization Content Library Download job has completed yet

questions.explanation: To determine if content has been downloaded from the Content Service, review the Hardware Model Content Service Download section on the Normalization and Content Service dashboard (C). This section shows the download status, last download date, and next scheduled download. The dashboard provides a consolidated view of the content service health and status for quick verification of content availability.

questions.stem: How do you prevent normalization information fora specific hardware model from being sent to the ServiceNow Content Service?

options.text: Select Exclude from content service on the Normalization tab of the hardware model record
Click the Exclude button on the hardware model record
Click the Opt-out button on the hardware model record
Select Opt-out from content service on the Normalization tab of the hardware model record

questions.explanation: To prevent normalization information for a specific hardware model from being sent to the ServiceNow Content Service, select 'Opt-out from content service' on the Normalization tab of the hardware model record (D). This opt-out setting ensures the model's data is not shared with ServiceNow's Content Service. The field is located on the Normalization tab, not as a button (C) or an 'Exclude' option (A, B).

questions.stem: What are the two primary benefits of deploying asset tasks during the retirement of an asset? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The two primary benefits of deploying asset tasks during retirement are: Reduces manual intervention (A) — asset tasks automate the data updates that would otherwise require manual changes; Increases data accuracy (C) — automated tasks ensure all relevant fields on asset and CI records are consistently updated. Reducing field agent training (B) and process cost (D) are secondary benefits. Increasing speed of updates (E) is a result but not the primary stated benefit.

questions.stem: A user’s broken laptop is replaced via an incident. Upon completion, the Incident Management application triggers the swap/replace asset task. Which fields are automatically updated in the associated asset record? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: When the swap/replace asset task triggers from an incident, the following fields are automatically updated: Software allocations (A) — licenses are moved from old to new hardware; Maintenance contracts (B) — contract associations are transferred; Related CI record (D) — the CMDB relationship is updated to reflect the new hardware. Depreciation values (C) are calculated independently per asset. Disposal information (E) would only update if the old asset is being retired, not swapped.

questions.stem: A transfer order is used to do what?

options.text: Move an asset to an external stockroom
Transfer an asset to a user

questions.explanation: A transfer order is used to move an asset between stockrooms (C). Transfer orders manage the movement of both consumable and non-consumable assets between company stockrooms within the organization. They don't transfer assets between vendors (A), to external stockrooms (B), or directly to users (D). The transfer order structure includes transfer order lines for each asset and transfer order line tasks for tracking each stage of the transfer.

questions.stem: What types of inventory audits are supported with the Hardware Asset Management (HAM) application? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: HAM supports two types of inventory audits: Stockroom audit (A) — auditing assets assigned to a specific stockroom; Location audit (C) — auditing assets at a physical location. Vendor audit (B) is not an inventory audit type — it's a procurement/compliance function. Discovery audit (D) is related to ITOM Discovery, not HAM inventory auditing. The two audit types align with the two ways assets are organized: by stockroom and by location.

questions.stem: Which of the following are valid contract states? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Valid contract states include: Draft (A) — contract is being created but not yet active; Active (B) — contract is in effect; Expired (E) — contract has passed its end date. 'In use' (C) is an asset state, not a contract state. 'New' (D) is not a standard contract state — contracts start in Draft. The contract lifecycle progresses through states like Draft, Active, Extended, Renewed, Expired, and Canceled.

questions.stem: Stockroom C has seven Bluetooth keyboards with a total value of $630. The asset manager procures two more of the same model keyboards for $360 and adds them to Stockroom C. When one of these keyboards is consumed, what is the value of the consumed Bluetooth keyboard?
questions.explanation: When consumables are merged, the system calculates a blended cost. Initially 7 keyboards at $630 total = $90 each. Adding 2 more at $360 total = $180 each. After merging: 9 keyboards with total value $990 ($630 + $360). Blended cost per keyboard = $990 / 9 = $110. When one keyboard is consumed, its value is $110 (A). The blended average ensures all items of the same type in a stockroom carry the same per-unit cost.

questions.stem: Which applications are required to perform a blind audit of your asset inventory?

options.text: Hardware Asset Management (HAM) and ServiceNow My Assets mobile app
Hardware Asset Management (HAM) and Software Asset Management (SAM)
ITSM Asset Management and ServiceNow My Assets mobile app
ITSM Asset Management and ServiceNow Agent mobile app
Hardware Asset Management (HAM) and ServiceNow Agent mobile app

questions.explanation: To perform a blind audit of asset inventory, you need Hardware Asset Management (HAM) and the ServiceNow Agent mobile app (E). HAM provides the audit framework and reporting, while the Agent mobile app (Now Agent) enables field scanning of assets. Mobile My Assets (A) is for end users to view their assets, not for auditing. SAM (B) is for software. ITSM Asset Management alone (C, D) doesn't include the full audit capabilities that HAM provides.

questions.stem: Within the asset audit form, where would you find the list of all assets that were found at the stockroom or warehouse that is being audited?
questions.explanation: Within the asset audit form, the list of all assets found (scanned) at the stockroom or warehouse being audited is in the Scanned assets related list (B). This list shows every asset that was physically scanned during the audit. Expected assets (C) shows what should be there based on records. Identified assets (A), Labelled assets (D), and Inventoried assets (E) are not standard related list names on the asset audit form.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of stock rules? (Choose two.)

options.text: To automatically transfer assets when a low quantity threshold is detected in a stockroom
To track stock orders from a vendor
To send notifications when a low quantity threshold is detected in a stockroom
To track stock movement between stockrooms
To send notifications when a stock shipment arrives at a stockroom

questions.explanation: Stock rules serve two purposes: automatically transfer assets when a low quantity threshold is detected in a stockroom (A) — by creating transfer orders for restocking; and send notifications when a low quantity threshold is detected (C) — emailing the stockroom manager about low inventory. Tracking stock orders (B), tracking movement between stockrooms (D), and notifications on shipment arrival (E) are not functions of stock rules.

questions.stem: Which of an organization’s assets are managed using stockrooms?

options.text: All available stock, consumable or not

questions.explanation: All available stock, consumable or not (A), is managed using stockrooms. Stockrooms in ServiceNow manage both consumable assets (like keyboards, cables) and non-consumable assets (like laptops, monitors). The stockroom is the organizational unit for all physical inventory regardless of asset type. Option B (just consumables) is too narrow. Options C (hardware and software) and D (disposable assets) don't accurately describe stockroom scope.

questions.stem: When using transform maps to transform imported hardware model data to your desired asset tables, what option do you set to uniquely identify the same asset in order to merge/update records?
questions.explanation: When using transform maps, the Coalesce (A) option is set on a field to uniquely identify the same asset for merging/updating records. When coalesce is checked on a field mapping, the transform uses that field as the unique key to find existing records — if a match is found, the record is updated rather than creating a duplicate. Consolidate (B), Unique identifier (C), Unique source (D), Unique target (E), and Combine (F) are not the correct ServiceNow term.

questions.stem: An event runs each night to send reminders to contract administrators about contract expiration dates (e.g., so they can renew or renegotiate the contract). By default, when does the contract administrator receive these notifications? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: By default, contract administrators receive expiration notifications at: 60 days before (C), Day of expiration (D), 90 days before (E), and 30 days before (F). These four notification intervals give progressively urgent reminders. 10 days before (A) and 1 week before (B) are not part of the default notification schedule. The standard intervals are 90, 60, 30 days, and day-of to allow adequate time for renewal or renegotiation planning.

questions.stem: Which of the following are valid contract states during a contract’s lifecycle? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Valid contract lifecycle states include: Draft (A) — initial creation; Canceled (B) — terminated before completion; Active (E) — currently in effect; Expired (G) — past end date. Renewed (C) is an action/transition, not a persistent state. Extended (D) modifies the active state's end date. Renegotiated (F) is not a standard contract state. The main lifecycle is Draft > Active > Expired (or Canceled), with possible extensions during the Active phase.

questions.stem: What are the key steps for importing asset data? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The key steps for importing asset data are: Load data (E) — import the source data into a staging table; Create transform map (D) — define field mappings from staging to target table; Run transform map (B) — execute the transformation to create/update records. Merge transform maps (A), Update transform map (C), and Consolidate data (F) are not standard import steps. The standard import set process is: load data, create/configure transform map, then run the transform.

questions.stem: What must exist before a consumable can be consumed? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Before a consumable can be consumed, the following must exist: A model record (B) — defining what the consumable is; A model category record (D) — categorizing the consumable type; A consumable record (E) — the actual inventory record in a stockroom. A stock order record (A) and transfer order record (C) are not prerequisites for consumption — consumables can exist in stockrooms without having been ordered or transferred.

questions.stem: When using the HAM application, what happens when you create a new transfer order line on a transfer order?

options.text: The asset(s) listed in the transfer order line are automatically transferred to the new stockroom
The transfer order line is automatically placed in a state of Ready for fulfilment
A transfer order line task is automatically created to move the transfer order line from one stage to another
A transfer order line task is automatically created to validate enough stock exists
The asset(s) listed in the transfer order line are automatically readied for shipment

questions.explanation: When you create a new transfer order line on a transfer order, a transfer order line task is automatically created to move the transfer order line from one stage to another (C). Based on the model category of the asset, default template tasks are generated. The assets are not automatically transferred (A) — tasks must be completed first. The line is not automatically 'Ready for fulfillment' (B). Tasks validate and track the transfer process through each stage.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow Mobile app provides end users visibility to their assigned hardware and consumable assets?
questions.explanation: The Mobile Agent App (D) — also called Now Agent — provides end users visibility to their assigned hardware and consumable assets. While Now Mobile also offers My Assets functionality, in the context of this question's options, Mobile Agent App is the closest match. Mobile Asset App (A), Mobile App (B), and Mobile ITAM App (C) are not actual ServiceNow mobile application names.

questions.stem: Select the three main components of the data certification process. (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three main components of the data certification process are: Create the certification filter (C) — defining which records to certify; Create the certification schedule (D) — determining when certification runs; Run the certification (E) — executing the certification process. 'Certify the certification' (A) is redundant and not a real component. 'Assign the certification tasks' (B) happens automatically during the certification run, not as a separate setup component.

questions.stem: Which catalog facilitates the ability to source from existing stock?
questions.explanation: The Product Catalog (D) facilitates the ability to source from existing stock. The Product Catalog contains all hardware and consumable models available in the organization's inventory, enabling fulfillment from existing stockroom inventory. The Service Catalog (C) is for requesting items. The Procurement Catalog (A) is not a standard name. The Vendor Catalog (B) is for external vendor sourcing, not existing internal stock.

questions.stem: From where can you publish catalog items? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Catalog items can be published from the model category (A) — which defines the catalog item template for all models in that category — and from a model (E) — which creates a specific catalog item for that product. Asset records (B) are instances, not product definitions. User records (C) have no catalog publishing function. Vendor items (D) are external and must be mapped through the Product Catalog first.

questions.stem: Publishing an item to the Service Catalog can be done by using the “Publish to Hardware Catalog” related link in:
questions.explanation: The 'Publish to Hardware Catalog' related link is found in the Product Catalog (A). The Product Catalog contains model definitions that can be published as catalog items to make them available for ordering. From a model record in the Product Catalog, the 'Publish to Hardware Catalog' related link creates or updates the corresponding service catalog item. Inventory Catalog (B), Asset Catalog (C), and Supplier Catalog (D) are not where this related link exists.

questions.stem: An asset is manually created from a purchase order before it has been shipped by the supplier. By default, the state of the asset is set to:
questions.explanation: When an asset is manually created from a purchase order before it has been shipped by the supplier, the default state is 'On order' (A). This state indicates the asset exists in the system but hasn't been received yet. 'In use' (B) means it's deployed. 'Awaiting delivery' (C) and 'Pending transfer' (D) are not default states for PO-created assets. The On order state accurately reflects that the item has been procured but not yet received.

questions.stem: How often are the tabs in the Hardware Asset dashboard updated?
questions.explanation: The tabs in the Hardware Asset dashboard are updated in real time (C). Dashboard reports and metrics refresh dynamically as data changes in the underlying tables. There is no daily scheduled job (A), hourly update (B), or 15-minute interval (D) that controls dashboard refresh. When asset records, normalization statuses, or audit results change, the dashboard reflects those changes upon the next page load or refresh.

questions.stem: What minimum role is required in order to use the Hardware Asset dashboard?
questions.explanation: The minimum role required to use the Hardware Asset dashboard is the asset role (A). The asset role provides read access to asset management modules including the dashboard. ham_user (C) and ham_admin (D) provide broader HAM capabilities. asset_manager (B) is a higher-level role. inventory_admin (E) is for inventory management. The basic asset role is sufficient for viewing the dashboard and its reports.

questions.stem: What information would you find on the Inventory tab of the Hardware Asset dashboard? (Choose three.)

options.text: New hardware assets found by audits
Hardware models up for end of life

questions.explanation: The Inventory tab of the Hardware Asset dashboard shows: New hardware assets found by audits (A) — assets discovered during inventory audits; Active stock rules (D) — current stock rules monitoring inventory levels; Open asset audits (E) — audits currently in progress. Hardware models up for end of life (B) appears on the End of Life tab. Hardware nearing end of warranty (C) and Requests requiring sourcing (F) appear on other dashboard tabs.

questions.stem: Which mobile app can users leverage to create assets, perform inventory audits, and receive assets?
questions.explanation: The Now Agent Mobile App (A) allows users to create assets, perform inventory audits, and receive assets. The Agent app is designed for IT professionals and includes barcode scanning, PO receiving, and audit functionality. Now Procurement App (B) is not a standalone app. Now Mobile App (C) is for end users. Now Onboarding App (D) is for employee onboarding. The Agent app is the operational tool for asset management tasks.

questions.stem: Several of your models are listed as Match Not Found on the Model Management tab of the Hardware Asset dashboard. What are the potential causes of this? (Choose three.)

options.text: The hardware model content has not yet been downloaded from the Content Service
Normalization could not match any of the three key fields in the hardware model form with a rule in the Content Service
Your hardware model form contains a good model number, but a badly formatted model name
You have opted out of the ServiceNow Content Service
A normalization rule for the hardware model does not exist in the Content Service

questions.explanation: Models listed as Match Not Found can be caused by: Content has not yet been downloaded from the Content Service (A) — no reference data to match; Normalization could not match any of the three key fields with the Content Service (B) — data mismatch; Model form has good model number but badly formatted model name (C) — formatting prevents matching. Opting out (D) would prevent normalization entirely, not produce Match Not Found. The three causes relate to content availability and data quality.

questions.stem: What original costs are involved in purchasing an asset and putting it into use? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Original costs involved in purchasing an asset and putting it into use include: Lease (A) — initial lease costs; Delivery (B) — shipping and handling to receive the asset; Storage (E) — initial warehouse/stockroom storage costs. Spare parts (C), Maintenance (D) are operational expenses incurred during the asset's useful life, not original purchase costs. Original costs are one-time expenses at acquisition, while operational expenses recur throughout the lifecycle.

questions.stem: A scheduled job runs nightly to determine if any rate cards need to be applied to generate expense lines. What is the name of the scheduled job?
questions.explanation: The scheduled job that runs nightly to determine if rate cards need to be applied to generate expense lines is Process FM Costs (C). This Financial Management cost processing job evaluates rate card configurations and generates the corresponding expense line records. Process CM Costs (A), Process Rate Cards (B), and Process Expense Lines (D) are not the correct job names for this cost processing function.

questions.stem: What is included in the total cost of ownership? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Total cost of ownership (TCO) includes: Original cost (B) — the initial acquisition cost (purchase price, delivery, setup); Operational expense (D) — ongoing costs throughout the asset's life (maintenance, repairs, support). Delivery cost (A) is a component of original cost, not a separate TCO element. Depreciation expense (C) is an accounting concept that reduces book value but is not an actual cash outflow added to TCO.

questions.stem: What is a requirement for sourcing a request from the requester’s local stockroom?

options.text: The requested stock must be in transit from a vendor
The requested stock must be available in the local stockroom
The requested stock must be available via transfer order from a remote stockroom
The requested stock must be in transit from a remote stockroom

questions.explanation: The primary requirement for sourcing a request from the requester's local stockroom is that the requested stock must be available in the local stockroom (B). The item must physically exist in the stockroom with sufficient quantity. Items in transit from a vendor (A) or remote stockroom (D) are not yet available locally. Transfer orders from remote stockrooms (C) describe a different sourcing method — the question specifically asks about local stockroom sourcing.

questions.stem: By default, what Quick links are available on the Hardware asset overview view? (Choose three.)

options.text: Assets eligible for refresh by model category

questions.explanation: The default quick links on the Hardware asset overview view include: Transfer orders (A) — for managing asset movements; Asset requests (C) — for handling incoming asset requests; Asset count by lifecycle state (F) — showing distribution across lifecycle stages. Assets eligible for refresh (B), Model normalization (D), and Asset count by model category (E) are available in other dashboard views or tabs but are not the default overview quick links.

questions.stem: A component is considered a configuration item (CI) as opposed to an IT asset when you want to:
questions.explanation: A component is considered a CI as opposed to an IT asset when you want to track its relationship information (C). CIs in the CMDB are defined by their relationships to other CIs and business services. Tracking incurred costs (A), managing retirement (B), and managing license contracts (D) are all asset concerns. Knowing who is using it (E) could apply to both, but relationship mapping is the defining CI characteristic that distinguishes it from asset management.

questions.stem: What is tracked throughout the life of an asset? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Throughout the life of an asset, the following data types are tracked: Financial data (A) — cost, depreciation, residual value; Contractual data (B) — warranties, leases, maintenance agreements; Lifecycle data (C) — state transitions from request through retirement. Configuration data (D) is CI-specific, tracked in the CMDB. Hardware data (E) is also CI-related operational data like CPU, memory, and OS. Assets focus on financial, contractual, and lifecycle tracking.

questions.stem: What is the focus of asset management?

options.text: Financial tracking of an organization's property
Financial tracking of the organization's network
Building the elements that create the organization's network

questions.explanation: The focus of asset management is financial tracking of an organization's property (A). ITAM centers on managing the financial aspects of assets — cost, depreciation, value, contracts, and procurement throughout the asset lifecycle. Option B (network tracking) is more aligned with network management. Options C and D relate to building/constructing, not managing existing assets. Asset management's core mission is financial accountability and lifecycle cost optimization.

questions.stem: Which tier of the capability blueprint focuses on achieving best-in-class?
questions.explanation: Strategic Conformance (C) is the capability blueprint tier that focuses on achieving best-in-class. As the highest tier (Tier 4), it represents the pinnacle of ITAM maturity where asset management is fully aligned with strategic business objectives. Trustworthy Data (B) is Tier 1 (foundation), Practical Management (D) is Tier 2 (basic processes), and Operational Integration (A) is Tier 3 (process integration). Best-in-class requires strategic alignment.

questions.stem: Which of the following are components of the ServiceNow asset lifecycle? (Choose three.)
