questions.explanation: Components of the ServiceNow asset lifecycle include: Procure (C) — acquiring the asset from a vendor; Request (D) — the initial request that starts the lifecycle; Receive (F) — physically receiving the asset into inventory. Discard (A) is not a standard lifecycle term — 'Retire' and 'Dispose' are used instead. Order (B) is part of procurement, not a separate lifecycle component. Install (E) is not a standard ServiceNow asset lifecycle stage.

questions.stem: What are the five valid phases of the Now Create methodology?
questions.explanation: The five valid phases of the Now Create methodology are Review, Prepare, Create, Validate, Recap (A). Now Create is ServiceNow's implementation methodology that guides customers through structured phases. The sequence starts with reviewing requirements, preparing the project, creating the solution, validating the output, and recapping results. Options B, C, and D use project management terminology not specific to Now Create.

questions.stem: What are types of assets? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Types of assets include: Software entitlement (B) — licenses and entitlements; Hardware (C) — physical equipment like laptops, servers; Consumable (D) — items used and depleted like cables, keyboards; Facility (F) — buildings and physical locations. Model (A) is not an asset type — it's a product definition. Stockroom (E) is a location where assets are stored, not an asset type itself.

questions.stem: What are the baseline asset lifecycle automation flows provided by the Hardware Asset Management (HAM) plugin? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The baseline asset lifecycle automation flows provided by HAM are: Hardware asset order (A) — for procuring new assets; Hardware swap order (C) — for swapping/replacing assets during incidents; Hardware retire order (D) — for decommissioning assets. Hardware bulk stock order (B) is not a baseline flow. Hardware deployment (E) and Hardware disposal (F) are stages within the lifecycle but not separate baseline automation flows.

questions.stem: What plugin helps alleviate inconsistencies in company names?
questions.explanation: The Normalization Data Services (B) plugin helps alleviate inconsistencies in company names. This plugin provides a normalization service that standardizes vendor and manufacturer names, ensuring consistent data across the platform. Extended CMDB (A) extends the CMDB data model. Contract Management (C) manages contracts. Data Certification (D) validates data quality but doesn't specifically normalize company names.

questions.stem: What are the Normalization statuses? (Choose six.)
questions.explanation: The normalization statuses are: Manufacturer Normalized (A) — only manufacturer matched; Match Not Found (B) — no match in Content Service; Partially Normalized (C) — some fields matched; Normalized (D) — fully normalized automatically; Manually Normalized (E) — normalized by user manually; New (G) — not yet processed. Version Normalized (F) and Found (H) are not standard normalization statuses. The six statuses track the progression from new through various levels of normalization.

questions.stem: An asset record tracks which data that is NOT part of configuration management? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Asset records track data NOT part of configuration management: Lifecycle data (A) — state transitions from request to retirement; Contractual data (B) — warranties, leases, maintenance agreements; Financial data (C) — cost, depreciation, residual value. Logical data (D) is not a standard category. Operational data (E) is tracked by CIs in the CMDB, not by asset records. The three asset-specific data types are financial, contractual, and lifecycle.

questions.stem: When selected on the model category form, what feature prevents the automatic creation of an asset?
questions.explanation: Enforce CI Verification (E) is the feature on the model category form that prevents automatic creation of an asset. When enabled, new CIs discovered for that model category require manual verification before an asset record is automatically created. This adds a quality gate to prevent unwanted asset proliferation. Enforce Asset Creation (A), Enforce Asset Verification (B), Enforce Asset Validation (C), and Enforce CI Validation (D) are not the correct field names.

questions.stem: In order for a hardware model to be fully normalized rather than partially normalized, what field is required in the hardware model record?
questions.explanation: For a hardware model to be fully normalized rather than partially normalized, the Model number (E) field is required. The docs state that for full normalization, you need manufacturer details AND a model number. If a model has manufacturer but no model number, it remains Partially Normalized. Name (B) is optional for normalization. Asset tag (C) is per-asset, not per-model. Display name (D) is auto-generated from normalization.

questions.stem: You have just created a new hardware model record for a group of laptops you purchased. When does normalization first run to normalize the record?

options.text: When the daily scheduled HAM – Daily job runs
When the weekly scheduled HAM – Normalization job runs
When you save the hardware model record
When you click the Normalize Hardware Model link under Related Links

questions.explanation: When you create a new hardware model record, normalization first runs when you save the hardware model record (C). Upon save, the system immediately compares the model data against the Hardware Normalization Content Service. The daily scheduled job (A) processes models in bulk later, and the weekly job (B) is not the standard schedule. There is no 'Normalize Hardware Model' related link (D) — normalization is triggered automatically on save.

questions.stem: When opted-in to the Hardware Asset Management Content Service, how often is updated content downloaded to the customer instance from ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: When opted-in to the Hardware Asset Management Content Service, updated content is downloaded to the customer instance daily (C). The Content Service synchronizes normalization data, lifecycle dates, and manufacturer information on a daily basis. Monthly (A), Weekly (B), and Quarterly (D) are not the default download frequency. Daily updates ensure instances have the most current normalization rules and product lifecycle data.

questions.stem: Normalization status is the level of normalization match based on what characteristics? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Normalization status is the level of match based on three characteristics: Model name (A), Model number (C), and Manufacturer (E). These are the three key fields used during normalization to match against the Content Service. If all three match, the status is Normalized. If only some match, status is Partially Normalized. Model category (B) and Display name (D) are not used in the normalization matching process.

questions.stem: As part of the hardware model normalization process, the Content Library automatically populates your inventory with what non-discoverable asset metadata?
questions.explanation: The Content Library automatically populates your inventory with manufacturer lifecycle dates (C) as non-discoverable asset metadata. Discovery can find specifications like part numbers and model info, but lifecycle dates (end-of-life, end-of-sale, end-of-support) come only from the Content Service. Manufacturer comparables (A), part numbers (B), and pricing (D) are not the primary non-discoverable metadata provided by the Content Library.

questions.stem: What core sets of data are required for effective IT asset management? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Core data sets required for effective IT asset management include: Manufacturers (A) — who makes the products; Locations (C) — where assets are deployed; Users (D) — who uses the assets; Models (F) — what products exist. Relationships (B) is primarily a CMDB/CI concern. Projects (E) is a PPM concern. The four core data sets define the who, what, where, and from-whom of asset management, forming the foundation for tracking.

questions.stem: What role is required to use the Hardware Model Normalization Overview dashboard?
questions.explanation: The ham_admin role (C) is required to use the Hardware Model Normalization Overview dashboard. This role provides administrative access to HAM features including normalization management, content service configuration, and the normalization dashboard. ham_normalization (A) is not a real role. ham_user (B) has read access but limited dashboard capabilities. asset_manager (D) and asset (E) don't include normalization-specific access.

questions.stem: When working in conjunction with a Field Service Management (FSM) change task, what feature removes the need to manually update the asset record associated to the task?
questions.explanation: Asset task (D) is the feature that removes the need to manually update the asset record associated with a Field Service Management change task. When an FSM work order or change task is completed, the associated asset task automatically updates the asset record fields (state, assigned to, location, etc.). This automation ensures asset data stays current without requiring manual intervention by the field technician or asset manager.

questions.stem: For what asset actions are asset tasks provided? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Asset tasks are provided for three asset actions: Provision (A) — deploying a new asset to a user; Retire (B) — decommissioning an asset; Swap (D) — replacing one asset with another. Update/Repair (C) is handled through incident or change management, not asset tasks. Assign/Allocate (E) is part of the provisioning process, not a separate asset task action. The three core asset task types automate the major lifecycle transitions.

questions.stem: What happens to the consumable's asset record after it has been consumed?

options.text: The record is marked inactive but remains in the system
The record state is set to In use
The record remains in the system for reporting purposes only
The record is removed from the system

questions.explanation: After a consumable asset has been consumed, the record state is set to 'In use' (B). The consumed consumable's record persists in the system with an In use state, reflecting that the item has been allocated to a specific user. The record is not removed (D) or marked inactive (A). While consumables are depleted when consumed, the record remains active for tracking and reporting purposes with the In use state indicating consumption.

questions.stem: A contract can be cancelled when the State is what?
questions.explanation: A contract can be cancelled when the State is Active (B). Only active contracts that are currently in effect can be cancelled. Expired (A) contracts have already ended naturally and cannot be cancelled. Inactive (C) and Rejected (D) are not standard contract states from which cancellation is available. Cancellation is an explicit termination of an active agreement before its natural expiry date.

questions.stem: During an inventory audit, what happens if you accidentally scan the same asset twice?

options.text: The most recent scan is imported

questions.explanation: If you accidentally scan the same asset twice during an inventory audit, HAM automatically removes duplicates (C). The system recognizes that the same asset tag or barcode has been scanned multiple times and deduplicates the scan results. It doesn't import both records (B) or only the first/most recent scan (A, D). The deduplication ensures accurate audit results without requiring the auditor to manually track what's been scanned.

questions.stem: A blind inventory audit is typically initiated via which interface?
questions.explanation: A blind inventory audit is typically initiated via the Now Agent Mobile app (C). The Agent mobile app provides the scanning capability needed for blind audits where the auditor scans assets without seeing the expected inventory list. Now Mobile app (D) is for end users, not for audit operations. Third-party API (A) and Now Inventory app (B) are not the standard interfaces for initiating blind audits.

questions.stem: Assets can be moved between stockrooms by using:
questions.explanation: Assets can be moved between stockrooms by using Transfer orders (D). Transfer orders are the mechanism for managing asset movement between company stockrooms, with transfer order lines for each asset and tasks for tracking progress. Stock orders (A) are for procurement. Stock rules (B) automate restock triggers but don't directly move assets. Transfer rules (C) is not a standard ServiceNow feature for stockroom transfers.

questions.stem: Describe the structure of a Transfer Order.

options.text: Transfer Order > Transfer Order Line > Transfer Order Task
Transfer Order > Transfer Order Task > Transfer Order Line
Transfer Order Task > Transfer Order Line

questions.explanation: The structure of a Transfer Order is: Transfer Order > Transfer Order Line > Transfer Order Task (B). The Transfer Order is the parent record, Transfer Order Lines specify individual assets being transferred, and Transfer Order Tasks are auto-created from lines to track each stage of the transfer. This three-level hierarchy ensures organized tracking from order to individual asset movement stages.

questions.stem: When running an asset audit, you receive the result of 10 "Expected and not found" assets. What does this mean?

options.text: You expected 10 assets in your inventory and scanned these 10 assets during your audit.
You scanned 20 assets in your inventory, but only 10 of them were on your expected inventory list.
You expected 10 assets in your inventory and scanned 10 assets during your audit, but none of them are on your expected inventory list.
You expected 10 assets during your audit inventory and scanned 10 assets, but none of them have a record in your ServiceNow instance.

questions.explanation: 10 'Expected and not found' means you expected 10 assets during your audit but they were not scanned — they are missing from the physical inventory (D). These assets exist in your records as assigned to the stockroom, but when you performed the physical audit, you couldn't find or scan them. Option A describes 'Scanned and expected'. Option B describes a mixed result. Option C incorrectly states they match — they specifically don't.

questions.stem: What requirements must be met in order for a consumable asset to be consumed? (Choose three.)

options.text: State is In stock or Pending Delivery

questions.explanation: For a consumable asset to be consumed, the following must be met: Quantity > 0 (A) — there must be stock available; Substate is Available (D) — the consumable must be in an available substate; State is In stock (F) — the consumable must be in the In stock state. Substate pre-allocated (C) means it's reserved for something else. Pending Delivery (B) means it hasn't arrived yet. Both B and C would prevent consumption. Stockroom threshold (E) is for stock rules, not consumption.

questions.stem: What are the main purposes of transfer order line tasks? (Choose two.)

options.text: To help track service levels and the time frame needed to complete a transfer order
To move transfer order lines from one stage to another
To help track the total number of assets moved from one stockroom to another
To automate reordering of consumables as they are consumed by users
To move transfer orders from one stage to another

questions.explanation: Transfer order line tasks serve two main purposes: helping track service levels and the time frame needed to complete a transfer order (A); and moving transfer order lines from one stage to another (B). Transfer order line tasks are the workflow mechanism that progresses lines through stages like shipment, transit, and receipt. Tracking total assets moved (C) and automating reordering (D) are not task functions. Moving entire transfer orders (E) is not what line tasks do.

questions.stem: What prevents two asset managers from transferring the same asset at the same time?
questions.explanation: A business rule (A) prevents two asset managers from transferring the same asset at the same time. ServiceNow includes a business rule that checks whether an asset is already on an active transfer order and prevents it from being added to another. This concurrency control ensures data integrity. Stock rules (B), stockroom rules (C), and transfer rules (D) are not the mechanism that enforces this constraint.

questions.stem: When should you retire an IT asset?

options.text: At any point it is recommended by the HAM-defined asset policy
At any point that it is recommended by your company-defined policies and procedures
At any point it is recommended by the HAM-defined asset disposal procedure
When the Hardware Content Service Lifecycle data reports the asset is nearing end-of-service
When the Hardware Content Service Lifecycle data reports the asset is nearing end-of-life

questions.explanation: You should retire an IT asset at any point that it is recommended by your company-defined policies and procedures (B). Retirement timing is governed by organizational policies that consider factors like age, condition, cost-effectiveness, and business needs. HAM doesn't dictate a universal retirement policy (A, C). Content Service lifecycle data (D, E) provides information but doesn't determine when to retire — that's a business decision driven by company policy.

questions.stem: What critical information should be tracked for your contracts? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Critical information to track for contracts includes: What each contract costs (B) — the financial terms and ongoing expenses; What assets each contract covers (D) — which specific assets are associated with each contract. Who purchased the assets (A) is procurement data, not contract-critical. What needs to be cancelled (C) is a management action, not tracking information. Tracking cost and coverage ensures proper financial management and asset-contract alignment.

questions.stem: Why may users request loaner assets even when the requested asset is not available in the local stockroom?

options.text: The request creates an automatic transfer order to move assets from a warehouse with in stock assets.
The wait-listed loaner asset requests provide visibility to streamline internal transfer order flows.
The wait-listed loaner asset requests provide visibility to the demand for loaner orders.
The request automatically creates a purchase order to obtain the assets from a vendor.

questions.explanation: Users may request loaner assets even when the requested asset is not available locally because the wait-listed loaner asset requests provide visibility to the demand for loaner orders (C). These requests help asset managers understand demand patterns and plan inventory accordingly. Auto-creating transfer orders (A) or purchase orders (D) is not the primary reason. Streamlining transfer flows (B) is close but doesn't capture the visibility/demand aspect.

questions.stem: Stock rules have automatic restocking actions that occur through a daily scheduled job. What plugin must be activated in order to configure and use the scheduled job?
questions.explanation: The Procurement plugin (B) must be activated to configure and use the stock rule scheduled job with automatic restocking actions. Stock rules with vendor-based restocking require the Procurement plugin because purchase orders and vendor item requests are procurement functions. Cost Management (A) is for financial tracking. Field Service Mobile (C) is for FSM. Order Management (D) is a broader commerce concept not specific to HAM stock rules.

questions.stem: Classes are represented as tables in the ServiceNow database. Which is the base asset class?
questions.explanation: The base asset class table in ServiceNow is alm_asset (C). This is the parent table for all asset types — hardware assets (alm_hardware), consumable assets, and license assets all extend from alm_asset. cmdb_asset (A) and cmdb_hardware (D) are not actual ServiceNow tables. alm_hardware (B) is a child table that extends alm_asset specifically for hardware assets. The 'alm' prefix stands for Asset Lifecycle Management.

questions.stem: Which view displays metrics to the user to indicate when they are due for a refresh based on the scheduled retirement of their assets?
questions.explanation: The My Assets view (D) displays metrics to the user indicating when they are due for a refresh based on scheduled retirement of their assets. This self-service view shows end users information about their assigned hardware including lifecycle status and upcoming refresh eligibility. Homepage (A), Home (B), and Overview (C) are general navigation pages that don't provide personalized asset refresh metrics to individual users.

questions.stem: Which of these automatic restocking actions are available in baseline? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a task assigned to stock room manager to contact procurement manager
Create a task assigned to the stock room manage to create a purchase order
Create a new asset from any returned inventory
Create a transfer order to restock from another stockroom
Create a transfer order to restock from a vendor

questions.explanation: The baseline automatic restocking actions are: Create a task assigned to stockroom manager to contact procurement manager (A) — notifying the manager to initiate procurement; Create a transfer order to restock from another stockroom (D) — automatically moving stock from another location. Creating purchase orders (B) requires the Procurement plugin. Creating assets from returned inventory (C) and restocking from vendors via transfer orders (E) are not baseline restocking actions.

questions.stem: When sourcing a requested item from a supplier using the catalog task form to create a purchase order, the catalog item must be available in:
questions.explanation: When sourcing a requested item from a supplier using the catalog task form to create a purchase order, the catalog item must be available in the Vendor Catalog (D). The Vendor Catalog contains items sourced from external suppliers with vendor-specific pricing and availability. The Product Catalog (B) is for internal model definitions. Supplier Catalog (A) and Inventory Catalog (C) are not standard ServiceNow catalog names used for this purpose.

questions.stem: What information would you find on the Procurement tab of the Hardware Asset dashboard? (Choose two.)

options.text: Hardware models up for end of life
New hardware assets found by audits

questions.explanation: The Procurement tab of the Hardware Asset dashboard shows: Hardware expenditure by vendor (C) — spending analysis across vendors; Requests that require sourcing (F) — open requests needing procurement action. Nearing end of warranty (A) is on the End of Life tab. Normalization status (B) is on the Model Management tab. Models up for end of life (D) is on the EOL tab. Audit findings (E) are on the Inventory tab.

questions.stem: Since trustworthy data is key to good asset management practices, where would you look to determine the number of days until next Content Service download will occur?

options.text: Asset Hardware Model Normalization > Content Service Setup

questions.explanation: To determine the number of days until the next Content Service download, look in Asset > Hardware Asset Dashboard (E). The Hardware Asset Dashboard includes Content Service status information showing download schedules and timing. Asset Administration (A) has general settings. Asset Overview (B) is a summary page. Content Service Setup (C) is for initial configuration. Asset Audits (D) is for inventory auditing, not Content Service status.

questions.stem: Which mobile app can users leverage to view the assets assigned to them and create incidents to report issues with their devices?
questions.explanation: The Now Mobile app (C) allows users to view their assigned assets and create incidents to report issues with their devices. This is the end-user mobile app that provides self-service capabilities including My Assets and incident creation. Now Agent Mobile app (A) is for IT professionals. Now Onboarding app (B) is for employee onboarding. Now My Assets app (D) is not a standalone app — it's a feature within Now Mobile.

questions.stem: When creating a stock rule that replenishes from a vender, what is primary requirement for the warehouse stockroom? (Choose two.)

options.text: The stockroom manager must have a valid email address
The stockroom must have an assigned manager
The stockroom must have an assignment group
The stockroom manager must have a valid mobile phone
The stockroom manager must have a valid time zone

questions.explanation: When creating a stock rule that replenishes from a vendor, the warehouse stockroom requirements are: The stockroom manager must have a valid email address (A) — for receiving restocking notifications; The stockroom must have an assigned manager (B) — someone must be designated to receive and act on restocking alerts. Assignment group (C), phone (D), and time zone (E) are not primary requirements for stock rule vendor restocking.

questions.stem: Which tab on the Hardware Asset Dashboard enables tracking asset models with missing purchase details?
questions.explanation: The Procurement tab (B) on the Hardware Asset Dashboard enables tracking asset models with missing purchase details such as pending deliveries and purchase orders. Procurement-related metrics including expenditure, sourcing needs, and purchase order status are all displayed here. Asset Health (A) is not a standard tab name. Model Management (C) focuses on normalization. Inventory (D) tracks stock levels. End of Life (E) tracks retirement metrics.

questions.stem: To utilize the contract rate cards features, which plugin is required to be activated?
questions.explanation: The Cost Management plugin (D) is required to be activated to utilize the contract rate cards features. Cost Management integrates with Contract Management to calculate costs based on rate cards and generate expense lines. Financial Management (A) is a broader concept. Contract Management (B) is already active by default but doesn't include rate card functionality. Rate Management (C) is not a ServiceNow plugin name.

questions.stem: The current value of an asset (original cost less the depreciated amount) is known as:
questions.explanation: The current value of an asset (original cost less the depreciated amount) is known as the Residual value (B). Residual value = Cost - Depreciated amount. For example, a $1000 asset with $500 depreciation has a residual value of $500. Cost of ownership (A) is the total expense. Current balance (C) is not the standard term. Salvage value (D) is the estimated value at end of useful life, which is a fixed estimate, not a calculated declining value.

questions.stem: Which of the following are considered original costs as opposed to operational expenses? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Original costs (as opposed to operational expenses) include: Warranty costs (A) — purchased upfront with the asset; Purchase price or lease cost (B) — the acquisition cost; Delivery costs (C) — shipping to receive the asset. Resource costs for support (D), Replacement parts (E), and Maintenance agreements (F) are all ongoing operational expenses incurred during the asset's useful life. Original costs are one-time expenses at the point of acquisition.

questions.stem: After installing the Hardware Asset Management (HAM) plugin, how do you update it when new versions become available?

options.text: The HI portal team automatically updates as new versions become available
On your instance, filter on application updates, then click Update
On your instance, filter on application updates, then request an update from HI
Run scheduled job, HAM Check for Updates, and request an update
Check the HI portal for updates and request an update

questions.explanation: After installing the HAM plugin, you update it by checking the HI portal for updates and requesting an update (E). The ServiceNow HI (Help & Information) portal is where instance administrators can view available plugin updates and request their installation. Automatic updates (A) don't apply to HAM. Application updates on the instance (B) apply to store apps. Scheduled jobs (D) don't check for plugin updates.

questions.stem: Baseline ITSM Asset Management provides which features? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Baseline ITSM Asset Management provides: Mobile My Assets (A) — end-user asset visibility; Stockrooms (F) — inventory location management; Mobile Asset Receiving (G) — receiving assets via mobile. Hardware Model Normalization (B), Asset Inventory Audit (C), Hardware Asset Dashboard (D), and Hardware Manufacturer Lifecycle Dates (E) are HAM-specific features that require the Hardware Asset Management plugin to be activated.

questions.stem: Taxes paid at the time of purchase are what type of cost?
questions.explanation: Taxes paid at the time of purchase are an Original Cost (D). Original costs are all one-time expenses incurred when acquiring and deploying an asset, including purchase price, delivery, setup, and taxes. Operating Expense (A) and Operating Cost (C) refer to recurring costs during the asset's useful life. Capital Expense (B) is an accounting classification for assets, but the question specifically asks about cost type, where 'Original Cost' is the HAM category.

questions.stem: Within the asset audit form, where would you find the list of all assets that are currently assigned to the stockroom or warehouse that is being audited?
questions.explanation: Within the asset audit form, the list of all assets currently assigned to the stockroom being audited is found in the Expected assets related list (B). Expected assets are populated from the existing records showing what should be in the stockroom. Scanned assets (D) shows what was physically found during the audit. Labelled assets (A), Inventoried assets (C), and Stored assets (E) are not standard related list names on the audit form.

questions.stem: When a hardware asset is retired what happens to any existing software allocations on that asset?

options.text: The software allocations remain with the hardware asset and need to be reclaimed manually
The software allocations are handled based upon the configuration of the system property glide.ham.retire_sw()
The software allocations are removed from the asset but not returned to inventory
The software allocations are automatically returned back into inventory

questions.explanation: When a hardware asset is retired, software allocations are automatically returned back into inventory (D). The HAM retirement process includes automatic reclamation of software licenses, making them available for reallocation to other hardware. They don't remain for manual reclamation (A), aren't removed without returning (C), and while option B mentions a system property, the default behavior is automatic return to inventory without needing separate property configuration.

questions.stem: Which are valid hardware model lifecycle phases? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Valid hardware model lifecycle phases include: General Availability (A) — the product is available for purchase and deployment; Pre-release (D) — the product has been announced but not yet available; End of Life (F) — the manufacturer has discontinued the product. Upgrade (B) is not a lifecycle phase. End of Subscription (C) applies to software/SaaS, not hardware. Beta (E) is a software development phase, not a hardware model lifecycle phase.

questions.stem: What functionality enables you to automatically create asset records from information provided by your vendor while your assets are still in transit?
questions.explanation: Advanced Shipment Notification (ASN) (A) enables automatic creation of asset records from information provided by your vendor while assets are still in transit. ASN allows vendors to send shipment details electronically, and ServiceNow creates corresponding asset records before physical receipt. Advanced Vendor Notification (B), Automatic Shipment Notification (C), Automatic Asset Notification (D), and Advanced Delivery Notification (E) are not the correct feature names.

questions.stem: During an audit, when is the Scanned Assets related list updated in the asset audit form?

options.text: When the nightly scheduled job runs
Each time scans are submitted from the app
Every time an item is scanned from the app

questions.explanation: The Scanned Assets related list is updated each time scans are submitted from the app (D). When auditors submit their batch of scanned items from the mobile app, the Scanned Assets list in the audit form is updated with the new entries. It's not updated by nightly jobs (A), every 15 minutes (B), every hour (C), or in real-time per individual scan (E). The update happens when scan batches are submitted/synced from the mobile application.

questions.stem: What is an attribute that will remain unchanged throughout the life of the asset?
questions.explanation: Serial number (D) is the attribute that remains unchanged throughout the life of an asset. The serial number is a permanent identifier assigned by the manufacturer that doesn't change regardless of upgrades, reassignments, or configuration changes. Memory (A) can be upgraded. Operating system (B) can be reinstalled or updated. CPU type (C) can potentially be upgraded. The serial number is the one immutable physical identifier.

questions.stem: During the hardware model normalization process, which field is the most important criteria for creating a fully Normalized hardware model?
questions.explanation: During hardware model normalization, the Model number (A) is the most important criteria for creating a fully Normalized hardware model. The model number serves as the primary matching key against the Content Service. Without it, a model can only be Partially Normalized even if manufacturer and name are present. Display name (B) is auto-generated. Manufacturer (C) is needed but the model number is the most critical differentiator. Model name (D) is optional.

questions.stem: Key features of consumables are: (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Key features of consumables are: Managed in bulk (B) — consumables are tracked by quantity rather than individually, with blended costs when merged; Low value (E) — consumables are typically low-cost items like cables, keyboards, and mouse pads. Consumables cannot be discovered (A) by network discovery. They are not retired on consumption (C) — their state changes to In use. Fixed cost (D) is incorrect — consumables use blended average costs.

questions.stem: What baseline flow could you use to replace hardware assets nearing their end-of-life?
questions.explanation: The Hardware Asset Refresh flow (C) is the baseline flow used to replace hardware assets nearing their end-of-life. This flow initiates the process of identifying assets due for replacement and creating the necessary requests and orders. Loaner Asset Refresh (A) is for temporary equipment. Update Asset Request (B) and Refresh Asset Request (D) are not the correct baseline flow names for this lifecycle transition.

questions.stem: Fixed assets refer to what type of assets?
questions.explanation: Fixed assets refer to Long-term assets (D). In accounting, fixed assets are tangible items with a useful life extending beyond one year, such as buildings, equipment, and machinery. They are capitalized on the balance sheet rather than expensed immediately. Current assets (A) are short-term by definition. Intangible assets (B) are non-physical like patents. Short-term assets (C) contradicts the nature of fixed assets. Fixed assets are synonymous with long-term tangible assets.

questions.stem: Which single view of the Hardware Asset Workspace provides a consolidated set of quick links to manage model normalization, asset requests, transfer orders, stock orders, refresh requests, and disposal orders?
questions.explanation: The Hardware asset overview (A) view provides a consolidated set of quick links to manage model normalization, asset requests, transfer orders, stock orders, refresh requests, and disposal orders. This is the main landing view in the Hardware Asset Workspace that gives asset managers quick access to all key functions. Inventory (B), Asset estate (C), Procurement (D), and Asset operations (E) are specialized views focused on specific areas rather than providing a consolidated overview.

questions.stem: When an employee leaves a company and their manager submits an Asset Reclamation Request for them which of their assigned assets are reclaimed by default?

options.text: All hardware and software assets but not consumable assets
All hardware, software, and consumable assets selected in the reclaim asset service catalog
All hardware software and consumable assets
All hardware and software assets selected in the reclaim asset service catalog

questions.explanation: When a manager submits an Asset Reclamation Request for a departing employee, all hardware, software, and consumable assets (C) assigned to that employee are reclaimed by default. The reclamation process covers all asset types to ensure complete recovery. Options A and D exclude consumables. Option B mentions selecting assets in a catalog, but by default, all assigned assets are included in the reclamation scope, not just selected ones.

questions.stem: What does the depreciation effective date field modify on the depreciation tab? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The depreciation effective date field modifies: Residual date (B) — when the asset reaches zero/salvage value; Depreciated amount (C) — the cumulative depreciation calculated from the effective date; Residual value (D) — the current value after depreciation. Salvage value (A) is set independently as the estimated end-of-life value and isn't modified by the effective date. Depreciation quantity (E) is not a standard field. The effective date is the starting point for all depreciation calculations.

questions.stem: What is the second tier of the capability blueprint?
questions.explanation: The second tier of the capability blueprint is Practical Management (A). The four tiers in order are: Tier 1 — Trustworthy Data, Tier 2 — Practical Management, Tier 3 — Operational Integration, Tier 4 — Strategic Conformance. Practical Management focuses on implementing basic asset management processes after establishing data quality foundations in Tier 1.

questions.stem: Which are assets? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Assets include: Servers (A) — hardware assets with financial tracking; Software entitlements (B) — license assets representing ownership rights; Facilities (E) — buildings and physical locations with financial value. Software distributions (C) are installable media/packages, not assets. Network cables (D) are typically consumables, not individually tracked assets. Servers, software entitlements, and facilities all have financial lifecycle tracking needs.

questions.stem: Which view within the Hardware Asset Management Workspace enables Asset Managers to work on features such as RMA request lines asset audits, disposal orders and stock orders?
questions.explanation: The Asset operations view (B) within the Hardware Asset Management Workspace enables Asset Managers to work on features such as RMA request lines, asset audits, disposal orders, and stock orders. This view consolidates operational tasks that require active management attention. Asset estate (A) shows overall asset status. Inventory (C) focuses on stock levels. Model management (D) focuses on model normalization and lifecycle data.

questions.stem: What information would you find on me Model Management tab of me Hardware Asset dashboard? (Choose two.)

options.text: Hardware models up for end of life
Hardware model purchase orders pending delivery
New hardware assets found by audits

questions.explanation: The Model Management tab of the Hardware Asset dashboard shows: Hardware model normalization status (B) — the current state of normalization across all models; Hardware models up for end of life (C) — models approaching their lifecycle end dates. Hardware nearing end of lease (A) is contract-related. Hardware model expenditure (D) is procurement-related. Purchase orders pending delivery (E) is on the Procurement tab. New audit findings (F) is on the Inventory tab.

questions.stem: What is required to manage utilization of the Hardware Asset Management Content Service?

options.text: The service must be opted in to and can be opted out of in the future, if required.
The service must be opted in to, but once enabled it cannot be opted out of.
A script must be defined to identify what information should be shared with the Content Service.
Nothing. The service is atomically enabled and cannot be opted out of.
The service is automatically enabled through the baseline installation but can be opted out of, if required.

questions.explanation: To manage utilization of the Hardware Asset Management Content Service, it must be opted in to and can be opted out of in the future if required (A). The Content Service is not automatically enabled — administrators must explicitly opt in. Once enabled, it can be opted out of if needed. Option B incorrectly states it cannot be opted out of. Options C, D, and E describe automatic enablement which is not how the Content Service works.

questions.stem: What is the first tier of the capability blueprint?
questions.explanation: The first tier of the capability blueprint is Trustworthy Data (C). This is the foundation tier that focuses on establishing accurate, consistent, and reliable data as the basis for all asset management activities. Without trustworthy data, higher tiers (Practical Management, Operational Integration, Strategic Conformance) cannot be effectively achieved. Data quality is the prerequisite for everything else in the ITAM capability blueprint.

questions.stem: Populating CMDB tables using import sets can inadvertently result in duplicate configuration items (CIs). To minimize this duplication, you can apply what process to the import sets?
questions.explanation: To minimize duplicate CIs when populating CMDB tables using import sets, you apply Identification and reconciliation (C) to the import sets. This process uses identification rules to match incoming data against existing records and reconciliation rules to determine how to handle matches (update vs create). Import set prioritization (A) and Transform map consolidation (D) are not standard features. Manual reconciliation (B) is not automated and doesn't scale.

Assets that are available only in the local stockroom are displayed and are available for selection
Assets are auto-allocated once the inventory is uploaded for a defined bundle
Assets are auto-allocated to the bundle as they are transferred into the stockroom
